tips.comment: Headmaster looks difficult to beat here. He was second, beaten 0.75 lengths on debut at Lingfield in May. He was then second again, beaten just a neck at Windsor last month. He should go one better here.
Grey Jaguar did well on debut after a duff start to get second. But that was when running against a 1-4 Fav. So with a better start and being second up, I would expect to see more improvement today.
Biplane today races off a pound higher mark than her last win, and with Joe Bradnam taking 3lb off, she looks a good e.w. Wasn't too far away when sixth of thirteen last time out.
13 times winner with the last win coming in September last year. Did finish 2nd at Ayr in May and holds an each-way chance if in the same form.

Disappointing favorite in a decent race last time, having shown promise on debut the time before. Probably the ground was too quick, and this better ground over a longer trip may see her get her head in front.
Awaafi won by nearly 3L and kept on well on debut in a C4. She drops to C5 today under penalty with a step up to 6f, which looks like it will suit after that run in.

I thought Arnaz was a touch unlucky when denied a clear run, finishing third of seven at Yarmouth on the penultimate start. Didn't get going until too late when fourth of seventeen last time out but ran on okay.

Justcallmepete ran well on its third start for the Tony Carroll yard. It was well fancied the time before but got no run. If he can repeat the form of that last run at Doncaster, he could gain his first victory for this yard.

Royal Musketeer returned from a short break to two decent runs, finishing third and then second on turf, both off a 68. Still on that mark today, but has a handy 7 lbs claimer onboard, which could be enough to get back on the top step.

Lord Abama looks quite a tempting price in this six-furlong handicap. He won at Thirsk last time, before the yard was in any kind of form. The second ran well after that at Doncaster, and the third won at Carlisle next time. He won that race off a mark of 70 and rises four pounds here. However, Rhys Elliott claims five pounds, effectively reducing the mark to 69. The yard has been flying this week, and I expect a very bold show.

Forever My Prince is an interesting runner in this grade. This three-year-old has already showed on turf at Newmarket and Windsor. A win at Lingfield on soft ground preceded this. Relatively unexposed compared to most, he has a chance dipping in grade.

Returned from a break with an eye-catching run in 6th on a decent handicap at Ripon in June and will certainly come on for the run. Got boxed in that day but ran on when in the clear and hopefully gets better luck today.

Talented sort who last won at Thirsk in April off a 4 lbs lower mark than today. Ran well when last seen over course and distance but wandered when hitting the front early. Shay Farmer (SR 25%) now claims 7 lbs and will likely be set a task of holding this horse a little later for his run. Capable, useful sort.

3-time winner for Rae Guest last season, who took a big step forward on the second start for Jack Jones when 4th at Chepstow last time. Down another lb, and another step forward should put her firmly in the mix this afternoon.

This horse is the rank outsider in this 9-runner field, but 25/1 to finish in the first 3 looks excellent value to me for this bottom weight in first-time blinkers. It's clear that the horse is a 6-furlong horse, so it was no surprise to see him bang there at this trip here last time out before fading in the final furlong. This is clearly going to be much more suitable, and he's been dropped another 2lb for that effort to 65. Some of his novice form would have him comfortably as a mid-70s horse, so he looks to have a great chance here, especially if the blinkers bring about any further improvement.

It was late last month when Paggane made his first appearance on the flat for new connections after being very useful under NH rules for Willie Mullins. He finished 3rd over an inadequate 12f and now, upped in trip, must surely enter calculations.

She did well last year but has not replicated that this year. Today's trip is likely to suit her. Also, any rain, and it is forecast, could be a help. Her best runs have come when the turf is softer. Each way bet.
Fingers crossed that Beauld As Brass has his sensible head on today, and there seems to be early money going on him this evening.
A horse coming back from a big break but does go well fresh, has the form to win this one and has been well backed in the market.

We haven't seen In the Breeze for a while. At the age of seven, he's been persevered with, and he's two wins from two visits to Haydock. Interesting stepping up further in distance for this yard. This race will likely reveal more of what ability remains.

A Richard Fahey trained 3-year-old who has had 5 races on the flat, winning once and has finished 2nd twice. She won in June in a class 6 handicap at Doncaster over 7f on good to firm going when made favorite, staying on well at the finish after a slow start to win by 1 1/4 lengths. She is in a class 5 fillies handicap over 7f on good going and has Oisin Orr in the saddle for the first time. She was only beaten a head last time out in a class 5 fillies handicap over 7f on good going when staying on at the finish, beaten by Pearly Squirrel (rival again today) who she is 1lb better off against. Has a decent e/w shout in this race today.

White Umbrella has been in good form on the all-weather, winning her last two races. It's always a risk expecting that form to be transferred to turf. However, White Umbrella did win on the turf at Catterick in 2023 and Chepstow in 2022. She won her last race by just under a length, which probably could have been more, so every chance the six-pound rise will be within her scope. All her six wins have been at six or seven furlongs.

Tsarina's Song can go well here in the last for the in-form Andrew Balding yard. It had shown promise in its maiden runs and was a beaten favorite on its handicap debut. It could certainly be involved in the finish here if getting some luck in running.

Three year old filly Sangara makes her turf debut. Her dam got off the mark, following plenty of unplaced efforts, in the July of her three year old season. Sangara's career best effort came over today's distance on a flat track. Haydock can suit. The ground may soften and this should be ok as the dam went well with give in the ground. The stable saddled a winner on Monday.

Maximum Scepticism looks very much the banker of the day judging by his two good maiden runs at the Curragh. He ran best of those on the far side when just over a length fifth behind Amadeus Mozart last time out and shouls improve on that.
A beaten favourite over 7 furlongs at Doncaster 3 weeks ago when a neck runner-up. The drop back to 6 furlongs should suit.
Bayraat was noted when running a good fourth on seasonal debut and is taken to strip fitter from that encouraging reappearance.

Showed promise on debut as a 2-year-old in France last year. Was then sold and moved to England, being placed in the Charlton yard. Made a good yard debut when 3rd by just over 2 lengths in a class 4, the winner of that being a smart-looking Sea The Stars prodigy. Form of that race has worked out well with the fourth, Cape Flora, who was 3/4 of a length behind and went on to score on Thursday, winning cosily by 6 lengths in class 5 company. She now gets the chance at the same company. Despite being unexposed to the ground, the pedigree points in the right direction. Sired by Nathaniel, a grade 1 winning horse who won the King George & the Eclipse, a top-class bloodline. Foaled out of Magnificent Style, a lightly raced useful grade 3 winner, so plenty of potential in this bloodline as she goes on to progress more.
On Key can win this. However, it's between him and Miss Hathaway. On Key is the quicker horse. He is 1lb higher, but he has all the attributes to get over the line. Strong contender.

Tim Easterby's Miss Hathaway ran some good races without winning as a juvenile, notably when beaten just a head in a Thirsk novice in June last year. She finally won at the tenth time of asking on her three-year-old debut at Pontefract in April. She then ran well from a poor draw to finish third in a Thirsk handicap last month, and the form of that race has worked out well, with the winner going in again and the fourth having won since.

Titian Blue has been holding her form in competitive 3yo sprint handicaps and wasn't disgraced off a higher mark last time. She eases a pound in the weights and represents the Mick Appleby yard, which does well with sprinters here. By Blue Point out of Galaktea, she's bred for speed on ground with a bit of cut, so the forecast for good to soft (in places) straight 6f at Nottingham should suit. Needs a small step forward on 2025 efforts, but with Frederick Larson booked and no standout exposed rival in the field, she's good value for the price.

Wise Approach won his first race at Ascot and has run well in better races. A Class 2 at York and the Norfolk Stakes at Royal Ascot, where he finished 2nd to Charles Darwin, should get his second win.
Amorim had a decent debut after a dodgy start in a C2 but still managed a decent second. Last time out, dropped to a C5 and won by a big 6L. I would expect more progress today while third up.

Not many with experience in this, but one that has, Sing The Blues, can make the most of that first run when she loomed up looking the winner at Yarmouth before hanging and finishing third. Could improve a ton for that.

Sapphire Steps is a 2yo colt trained by Richard Hannon. He is out of a dam yet to produce any foals to win but is out of a dam and grand dam that produced 38 wins, seven of which placed or won pattern races. He is a 38,000gns yearling. Dam Hidden Steps was a 7f/1m winner and won on debut as a 2yo, so quite forward in her condition. The yard won this in 2020 and 2022. Interesting at 12-1 under Sean Levey for a trainer that has picked up 70 winning 2yo at Newbury.

Wondrous makes her debut in a race that lacks standout experience. She's bred to be useful - by Acclamation out of Qafilah, a mare who stayed a mile well. Trained by a yard that does well with 2YO newcomers, especially on quicker ground, and drawn to get a good position if she breaks smartly. Decent price offered, all things considered.
Has shown plenty of promise in 2 starts to date, finishing 4th on each occasion, including over this course and distance last time. Improvement likely and holds an each-way chance.

Daughter of little-known sire Sergei Prokofiev, this filly. Trainer Meehan is firing, and so too is jockey Charles Bishop, an experienced horseman who should suit this horse. Has drawn out, so deserves to be at longer odds on that score over this trip. But with a bit of luck and held up for a last run at them, could be in the frame.
Rod Millman and Hollie Doyle combine here, and both are going well in the last fortnight. Drawn to take advantage and is by sprinting sire Blue Point, so looks well suited to the trip.
Expensive yearling who is making debut for a yard that has been in good form with its 2-year-olds. Will have been well prepared and should be there or thereabouts.

Art Lover had a duff start on debut in a C3 at 6f but will be all the better for that run. With today's step up to 7f and dropping to C4, it's likely to suit if getting a better start, with more expected today EW.

Lost Signal is a 2yo colt trained by Richard Hannon, who won this race last year. Lost Signal is out of a dam, Smile At Me, sired by Galileo, who has yet to produce a winner. However, her dam and grand dam produced multiple winners, amassing 24 wins, which includes some useful sorts. Curly (sired by Galileo) is rated 108, and more notably, Danehill Dancer is rated 118, a top-class 2yo, then a smart sprinter who went 1-1-1-2, winning two Group 1's at the Curragh and Leopardstown as a 2yo. Lost Signal could produce an effort to play a big part in proceedings today for Richard Hannon who will have his colt primed and ready.
Was a little disappointing on debut when only 13th of 18. Should be better than that race showed, and with improvement likely for having had that run, holds an each-way chance.

Golden Handshake's figures of -921 tell the story of progression and now look straight. It was only a maiden he won (but was 2/11), but it was a good straightener for this handicap debut for Haggas and Marquand. Odin Legacy is consistent and forward enough to make it a fight.

Bownder can go well for the Jonathan Portman yard with young Oliver Tubbs on board, claiming 5lb. He ran below form last time in a four-runner race, but now back in distance, he could bounce back to the form he showed the race before when winning over this trip.

Lady Of The Isles is a 3-year-old gelding trained by Heather Main. He is improving with each run; 36-58-63. Rossa Ryan retains the ride now handicapping. Interesting, particularly as Rossa Ryan is 5/23 wins for Heather Main, a trainer who has been amongst the winners of late: Iconic Times 13-2 and Believe You Me 8-1. She has also picked up 12 winners at Newbury, showing a LSP of £233.50. Her Lady Of The Isles is a third foal related to Island Bandit (6 wins, winning twice at Newbury at 125-1 and over CD at 3-1) and Brave Call (1 win) 88-86, both trained by Heather Main. Chance!
Was a winner at Wolverhampton in February and has finished 2nd in 3 of 5 races since. Likely to go well again and should be there or thereabouts.

Darn Hot Mystery was placed in all 3 starts as a two-year-old but disappointed on seasonal debut at Nottingham in May when running as though badly needing the run when finishing last. She dropped 2 lbs here and could look a decent each-way bet if she can return to last season's form.

Thiscouldbefun got her first win back in April but took on weight for that and has had two down-the-pack runs since. She has dropped in weight and is now just 1 lb above that last winning mark and gets Billy Loughnane this time, so I would expect more EW.

I'm happy to take the view that it was the soft ground which was to blame for a poor run from the horse last time out on debut for a new stable. There's enough evidence on a maiden run and a novice run which suggests she's way too big here. Her 2nd in a novice race has mid-70 types horses around her in 1st, 3rd, and 4th, so the fact she races off 67 here suggests she could be competitive. It was a similar story with the third place in a maiden too, so perhaps she shouldn't be overlooked on that evidence.
The step up in trip produced another worthy performance from the consistent Orchard Keeper at Goodwood five weeks ago, and she can follow up over this extended trip.

This horse was very impressive on debut winning in taking fashion.
Carries a 7lbs penalty in this race, but should win this comfortably before being raised in class.
Showed some ability in 2 races when trained by Charlie Appleby. Makes debut for new yard and holds an each-way chance if building on those previous races.

Twice raced gelded son of New Bay & Phillipine Cobra ( Dam's sire Showcasing ) who was last seen at Ffos Las 17 days ago where finishing 4th/8 drops back down in trip here racing at the 1 mile trip that being a good move by his connections as he didn't look ready to tackle the 1 mile 2 furlong trip last time out however having gained experience and fitness from that second outing after his 243 day break having changed yards in the process of that break D P Quinn's new recruit can be a whole different proposition this time out and is most certainly open to plenty of progress at this stage and this class 4 Novice Stakes race looks a straightforward assignment for this individual jockey J F Egan takes the ride and can give Zolder a promising ride here at Newmarket price at the time of writing represents good E/W value and a frame finish at the very least wouldn't be so bad on this occasion worth the E/W shout

The James Owen-trained Asmen Warrior was 2nd on his seasonal debut to Convergent, who has gone on to be beaten a nose in the German Derby and is now rated 112. The 3-year-old Saxon Warrior gelding gets the weight allowance, and off a mark of 85, he must have every chance in this 7-runner C4 handicap.

We've seen these sorts before, but I just think GISELLES DEFENCE either gets withdrawn, and we get our money back, or is given another whirl straight after yesterday's win and will see some market support. Worth backing with that in mind.

We've backed her on her last two runs, both solid seconds, and she's ready to strike. Despite being top weight after a 3lb rise for her latest effort when beaten by a neck in a class 2 at York last month, she's now dropped into class 3 in a much weaker race. She's improved on each run since debuting in England, and I think she still has a lot of potential going forward, so I feel her mark is still rather lenient. Conditions are well within her favor, and if replicating her previous runs coming off the pace and getting a clear path unlike last time, she could be hard to peg back on the line to home. A first-time booking of Jason Watson on this filly, he's in good recent form and has a 17% strike rate at the July course. So hopefully a wise choice of booking for the Sangater yard.

Was well beaten in a big field over 1m at Ascot last month but wasn't beaten far when finishing just outside the places in fourth when dropped back to 7f here six days ago. Further drop back in trip should suit. Should be involved at the finish.

Steph Hollinshead's front runner, Angel Shared, should be capable of winning this mediocre handicap off a three lb higher mark than the one of 78 that she carried when winning over this C&D last month, provided Dougie Costello can once again get her to behave and go into the stalls.

This J & T Gosden-trained filly did well to only be beaten 1 1/2 lengths in second behind the Edward Smyth-Osbourne-trained Tavanadespite, showing signs of greenness over seven furlongs on good ground at Haydock 14 days ago. With Benoit D L Sayette booked to ride, she must hold every chance of a win today.
Down in grade (Class 3 to 4) and off the same mark (69) as when beaten less than 1 length last run. CATCH CUNNINGHAM should more than be in the mix here. NAP
The ease in grade to Class 4 should suit after racing in a Class 2 at Sandown over this trip last time out when going fourth close to home despite losing a shoe.

A close contest on paper, but Night on Earth looks overpriced relative to his rivals here at 6/1. He has run some solid races here in the past, lurks on a dangerous mark, and has shaped better than the bare result lately. Eased in grade, Joe Leavy is up for the first time since his last win and eased in grade, looks the pick.

JACQUELINA has gone from a 40/1 shot to favorite in five days and has stayed at the same mark, so we could get anything here. She was mid-division in a higher grade and not beaten far the run before last, so is chanced at this price.

Not much to choose between Outrun The Storm and ENPASSANT. However, preference is for the latter, off the same mark as last run when placed less than 1 length behind and has the 'hare' (likes to lead) of Outrun The Storm to set him up here.

Was well beaten over today's trip at Leicester in May but improved to finish a close second (by a neck) over the same trip at Chester last month. Won this race two years ago off 3lb higher. Should be thereabouts.
Won over the extended mile at Nottingham last time out and just a pound higher today. The drop back to 7 furlongs will suit with an expected fast pace.

Still a maiden after 5 runs coming from 6-8f . Is running over 7f today & has dropped from an opening handicap mark of 67 to 65 . Is wearing a 1st time tongue tie which could produce a better performance with the S.C.Williams yard who's string have been running well over last month .
Won a couple of times last year, enjoys the fast ground and the distance, may improve a bit and looks an attractive price.

This J & T Gosden trained 3-year-old colt has won his first two races over one mile at Wolverhampton and one mile two furlongs on good to soft ground at Windsor 39 days ago. When going clear in the closing stages, he easily beat the A M Balding trained Jupiter Ammon by four lengths. So with Oisin Murphy back onboard, he can complete the hat trick tonight.
Ascending Star finished ahead of Lucky Hero when 3rd at Chester in his only start running on after a slow start and he should confirm that form at Hamilton over a stiff six furlongs.
Showed some promise on debut in April when 4th of 12 but failed to build on that next time. Should be better than that latest run showed, and any improvement gives an each-way chance.

Double Rush is a very short price in this competitive handicap. However, he looks like a three-year-old who is progressing quickly. His third in the valuable handicap at York just before Royal Ascot was an excellent performance, and he runs off the same mark here. With the age allowance and a little bit of luck in this big field, he can step forward again.

50-race veteran Bergerac has 8 wins and 13 placed finishes to his name. His last win came here at Hamilton over 5 furlongs last month. He followed that with 4th of 14 at Newcastle off 4 lbs higher. He steps back up to 6 furlongs here, a distance he has won at 3 times, and looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

Worth an each-way bet on this improver who won 3 starts back and has improved in defeat on his 2 starts since. A stiff 6f is ideal for him as he does stay further than this. This will be a test of 6f stamina with a strong pace expected, and as such, the race will be run perfectly for him.

Northern Ticker has yet to hit top gear this season but shaped as if needing the run when down the field at York in a tough handicap. He's now dropped in grade and gets the assistance of a leading apprentice, which could signal intent. With prior placed form in decent company and a mark that's edging into more workable territory, he's not one to dismiss lightly if bouncing back to his earlier winning ways.
At the foot of the weights and back down to a winning mark. Had a wind op since last run here which was an eye catching staying on 4th over 5f. Decent high draw and won't mind any rain.

COMMANCHE FALLS runs well here at Hamilton and is considered at a big price here. Last time out, the run here was from this mark with today's jockey on board and was a narrow second-placed finish. The stable has come into decent form, and he's potentially able to get involved at a big price. Not drawn out of it and will get a pace to aim for if there's a gap.

Sophia's Starlight did win two C2 on the trot last autumn after a similar break to today, with the second of those being off a 93. Although not great for the last two runs, the first was in listed company and the second in a C2 was on the AW, which has historically never gone well. I think today's return to C2 on turf off a 95 after a break could be worth an EW 4P.
Khuskhas won a maiden well last time, and that form looks strong with the runner-up winning since. Open to plenty of improvement too.
Won decisively last time and is turned out under a penalty here. This step up in trip will see her to even better effect.

This could be one for the Michael Dods team. Educating Rita was given a couple of very stern tasks at the end of her two-year-old season and wasn't good enough. She hasn't set the heather alight so far this year, but with the yard being mostly out of form, she probably hasn't been able to shine. This doesn't look like a strong handicap, and I quite like the look of her chances at a very fair-looking price.
All three career wins have been at Newcastle on the all-weather. Runs off a lower turf mark tonight and should be there or thereabouts.
Classy Al just strikes me as an older sort who seems to be running well and is therefore considered. Given a look at a favored course with a favored jockey to boot.

The 4-year-old hasn’t landed a blow this year, but she hasn’t been disgraced. His six runs this year have been in class 3, 4, and 5 company, now running in a class 6 handicap. A good claiming apprentice is booked for the ride, and he’s effectively now 16 lb lower from his spring return mark. He could be ready to strike.
Wasn't beaten far when finishing second over C&D last month but not in the same form on his last two starts. Is a two time course winner over 5f. Should be involved at the finish.

The 6-year-old ran a big race last week and is in good shape. He lost by a neck in a high-quality 17-runner £52K handicap and gets to run off the same mark in this £9K handicap. Plenty of miles on the clock, but I like his C/D stats: five runs, three wins, and a defeat by a nose. Drawn in stall 1 for this 5f dash won’t do any harm.
Winner on second start for Mark Walford at Thirsk in May. Very solid efforts in defeat since and is clearly in good heart at the moment so should run very well once again.

The 3yo was a good 3rd of 13 on his debut, decent rating, the 4th has run a couple of good races since, will be fresh after an 8 week break, most of his rivals in this novice stakes have shown very little on the track so far. He should be able to get a good early position from stall 1 for this 6f sprint.

Ran well to win over C&D ten days ago when returning from eight months off. Should be fitter today. Has won one and placed in two of his five starts since joining this yard last year. Should be thereabouts.

It has been a while since we have seen the best of him. However, he ran an improved race at both Doncaster and Haydock on June 2nd and 4th. Hopefully, he can improve on those two outings this evening.
Has run some good races this year, winning at Wetherby and Leicester. Disappointing last time out, but could bounce back at big odds.

The 5yo has 4 wins from 16. Two fair runs this year and his fitness should be better now. He’s on a handy mark now going off his form from last year. Good apprentice in the saddle and his 5lb claim should improve his chances.

A better effort from the 3yo two weeks ago, off the pace at the back but he moved nicely to challenge inside the final 2f, outpaced at the finish but he didn’t have the best track position. Something to build on. On a decent looking mark. Facing lower rated rivals now. The shorter trip could help him. He’s taking on older runners for the first time and his 8lb age allowance could be a factor.
Short of room over Beverley's extended mile when 5th of 7 last month and remains on the same mark with the slight drop in trip of appeal.

The 6yo ran a decent race under a very inexperienced apprentice four weeks ago. Plenty to like about his previous race, over this 12f C/D, when a very close 2nd of 5 runners. Same mark and jockey for this handicap. His four rivals that day were rated 81-87. One rival rated 74 in this handicap, the rest rated 67 or lower.

Nurburgring is yet to win a chase in four attempts but was a close 4th of 19 at the Cheltenham Festival in a competitive handicap chase and has since finished a neck 2nd of 20 at Royal Ascot in the two miles four furlongs Ascot Stakes. This looks a good opportunity for his first chase win.

The model I run suggests Amanha can win this one. This result has been driven by Amanha having a comparably high RPR to the other runners in this smaller 5-horse field. Comes into this having shown some form with figures of 4010-1 and needs to show a bit more to get over the finish line first here. Weight differential is small but 7 lbs in favor and a 2m 1f trip on yielding to soft. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Amboyna can win this one. This result has been driven by Amboyna having the highest RPR of this larger 14-horse race. Goes out with the highest weight to carry but only a small weight differential across the board. Last out 40 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Of major interest now moved up in trip. Improved on handicap debut last time and will do even better at this trip. Decent chance in this.

Just a tentative each way on Jim Bolger’s LONGWINDED LADY, who improved for the step up to 1 mile 4 after a few goes at 6 & 7 furlongs. While further improvement is required, the good to firm and the extra furlong might eke that out. The handicapper has shaved off 3 lb for that run, and Declan McDonagh has stayed loyal. There’s probably a bit of improvement to come, so I’ll chuck a penny in the well.

The model I run suggests Felicity Smoak should win this one. This result has been driven by Felicity Smoak having the highest RPR of this 7-runner field and is not overly penalized for it in the weights. Steps out carrying the lowest amount of weight around this 2m 1f round trip and can go on to get over the line first. Weight differential of over 8 lbs. Model has issued a 'low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Coole Cherry is a 7-year-old daughter of Mahler ex Cherry Black who traces back to Bright Cherry, who was the dam of Arkle by Archive. She finished second on four occasions in bumpers before winning her 3m maiden hurdle at 3/1 at Kilbeggan last September. She runs here in this 2m6f handicap hurdle off a mark of 113. She's been off the course for some time and now makes her return in the hands of P Townend for WP Mullins and the Blue Blood Racing Club. Off this mark, I think she may get back to her winning ways.

Eric McNamara's 5yo is the one I want to be with following his maiden win in May at Tipperary. He was value for far more than the official distance of a head, and soft ground ought not to be a problem on breeding.
Has been disappointing in 3 races since winning at Dundalk in November. Needs to rediscover that form, but that would give an each-way chance.

The model I run suggests Gaelic Arc can win this one. Gaelic Arc lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 10-horse field and looks to build on some solid form of late. Figures of 88-94 show some clear improvement and if anywhere near the same as the last win, can go close. Harry Sexton on board takes off a further 7 lbs, which is helpful around this 2m 1f trip. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Points winner who was a winner over fences for the first time at Limerick in May. No surprise to see following up if in the same form.

The model I run suggests Kalnoo can win this one. Kalnoo lines up here with a comparably high RPR to the other runners in this larger 15 horse field, but has an official ranking that leaves him well treated off this mark. Steps out carrying only 6 lbs more than the bottom weight but over 2 stone less to the top weight. Plenty of placing ability with figures of 33-435 but needs to show some more improvement to get over the line first. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Likable Chancer looks a big price at 33/1 based on his best form over fences. He was unplaced in his two runs this season on the flat and over hurdles but returns to fences off a 1lb lower mark than when second at Thurles in November. His last win was at Ballinrobe in September last year, and he was then placed in 3 of his next 4 starts over fences. With 4 places on offer, he looks to be worth an each-way bet.

A very well-stacked pedigree colt who I was tracking before debut. Wasn't overly impressive the first time out but made all on his second attempt when led start to finish before being pegged late on by a very promising looking A.P. O'Brien colt. So a massive improvement from that, and could take another step forward here. Hasn't got the best of draws but if he breaks well and replicates his previous run, he could be a hard one to catch.
Well-informed Chris Hayes takes the mount for the first time with a 26% strike rate in the last two weeks. The yard is looking in good shape and should manage to bag a winner to break the maiden tag early on.
Still learning when a decent 3rd last time. Connections are putting off the temptation of handicapping for now and keeping him in maiden class. Can win one of these.

Won his last 2 races, both over course and distance, and comes here from 7lb higher on a hat-trick bid. Showed a good attitude in winning last time, pulling well clear with the runner-up, and with the 4th home winning next time, looks decent form. Worth keeping onside in HT bid.

Tartaraghan won for the first time in her 25th start at Navan last Sunday. She won comfortably there by 1.25 lengths, taking advantage of her lowest handicap mark of 56. She has gone up 6 lbs for that win but had been placed twice off higher marks and was also second when she last ran at Down Royal in September last year. She looks like a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.

With two short prices at the front of the market and with four places up for grabs, there could be each way value in backing Smaoineamh Sile at 33/1. He won well on his penultimate start but disappointed last time out. The race probably came too quick for him. The step up in trip today is a big plus.
Has shaped well over a longer trip on her last two runs, both runs in higher grades than this race. Nudges up a pound and drops back to 13f, which will be her optimum trip.
Has only raced 4 times but has won twice and finished 2nd twice. Remains open to further improvement despite a 6 lb rise. No surprise to see following up.
Improving since moving to the De Bromhead stable and was well-backed when staying on nicely to win here LTO over 10f. The 2nd has won since, so a 6lb rise looks fair and worth a go over this trip.
A 4-time winner who has 2 of her 4 starts this year, both times over 1m4f. Finished 7th of 12 last month but could bounce back today with a good apprentice knocking off a handy 3 lbs.
In good form over hurdles and was going well when falling at Tipperary in his last appearance over fences. Still off a reasonable mark.
Hurdles winner who won over fences in December but has failed to build on that in 6 races since. Needs to rediscover that form to hold an each-way chance.
Won a couple of chases 2 years ago but not shown much since. Off a good mark today, and if recapturing old form, is weighted to go close in what looks a wide-open race.

The model I run suggests an upset from Robin De Roost. This result has been driven by Robin De Roost having the highest RPR of this larger 15-horse race but an official ranking that allows him to carry the joint lowest weight around this 2m 1f trip. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Beir Bua can win this one. Beir Bua lines up with the highest RPR in this limited experience race and has Mr. Ryan on board, relieving 5 lbs of weight for claiming. Also, it goes out carrying the lowest initial amount of weight, with 4 lbs less than the other runners. Experience can be important in these affairs, and Beir Bua had a good 2nd and 4th when last out. Looks to come on from those experiences and get over the line first with some improvement. The model has issued a 'moderate' stake indicator, which translates to a 1pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Yet to win from 12 starts but has placed in 2 of the last 5 outings. Only first reserve but holds an each-way chance on recent form if getting a run.
Is still a maiden after 8 starts but ran well when 5th of 15 over 6f at Naas just 12 days ago, faring best of those drawn on the wrong side. If building on that effort, could go well at decent odds.

Ciaran Murphy's 3 year old British Gelding THERUSSIANCOMPOSER runs here off bottom weight dropping another 2lbs & is now 9lbs lighter for his penultimate run here in Northern Ireland where he ran a career best 4th over today's trip. Previous experience up this hill certainly helps in my opinion so this Son of SERGEI PROKOFIEV has that to fall back on. Jockey Patrick McGettigan takes the reins & is very good value for his 7lbs. The draw in stall #13 isn't ideal but this charged fared ok from Stall #11 when last seen here, it is what it is but with such a big weight drop (when including Jockeys claim) at this big price of 33/1 this is too much for me to pass up & yes it's very likely to blow up in my face but this lad is dropped back in trip & I'll take my chance S he returns back to the scene of his career best performance feather light.

Sure to stay further than this and was very much over an inadequate trip last time. This is his 3rd and qualifying run before going down the handicap route. Could be saved for handicaps over further, but worth an each-way bet in this in the hope that he will be ridden to best advantage.

Cheekpieces are applied for the first time to Femme Beauty in this 7 furlongs maiden. Quite an open race in terms of form. Ken Condon trained filly by Ghaiyyath was disappointing on soft ground at Roscommon last time. Decent run at Fairyhouse on penultimate start. Could have a shout here. Ronan Whelan rides.

Invincible Will is an upset chance here as he wasn't suited last time by the tight track at Bellewstown. But before that, he was a useful sixth on debut at Navan. With the benefit of those two runs under the belt, he looks the improver in this field at odds. I like that the in-form trainer ran him over a mile last time out and that he was too keen on debut for his own good over six furlongs. This indicates that seven furlongs might be his trip, and with that extra stamina from the mile outing to benefit, he might stick on better this time of asking.

Henry De Bromhead is better known as a trainer of jumpers, of course, but his record of 40% with flat runners in the last fortnight has to be greatly respected here. Some each-way value is possible here with Monocle Rocket, who, while still learning his craft, could bob up at big odds for the astute veteran trainer. Jockey Slattery is also in good touch in the last fortnight, and this combination could surprise.

It's disappointing to say this, but this looks like one of the weakest, if not the weakest, Group 1s of the season. No overseas challengers, so it's the Oaks winner taking on horses she had 6 lengths or more behind her on that occasion. It's virtually impossible to see her being beaten with Whirl swerving the race, and she ought to be winning this very easily.
